findings.evidence: grep for `mem_toPreAbstractSimplicialComplex` returns nothing in `mathlib/Mathlib/` or `code/TauCeti/`; Basic.lean:174 defines a distinct `SetLike (AbstractSimplicialComplex ι)` instance from :55. The sibling file `LinkStar.lean` contains no `change`/`show`, so this is a new pattern introduced by this PR, not house style.
findings.fix: State the bridge once as a documented `@[simp] theorem mem_toPreAbstractSimplicialComplex {K : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι} {σ : Finset ι} : σ ∈ K.toPreAbstractSimplicialComplex ↔ σ ∈ K := Iff.rfl` (the single sanctioned defeq site, alongside the existing `join_toPreAbstractSimplicialComplex`), then replace each `change` with `simp only [← mem_toPreAbstractSimplicialComplex, join_toPreAbstractSimplicialComplex]` or `rw`. That confines the defeq to one auditable declaration and makes all five proofs survive any future change to how `AbstractSimplicialComplex` coerces.
findings.issue: `change σ ∈ (join K L).toPreAbstractSimplicialComplex ↔ _` silently crosses the wrapper: `AbstractSimplicialComplex` and `PreAbstractSimplicialComplex` have separate `SetLike` instances (Mathlib Basic.lean:55 and :174), and the identification holds only by structure-projection defeq. There is no comment explaining why. The same undocumented `change` recurs at lines 158, 165, 172, 179 — five instances of one pattern. The trailing `exact PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.mem_join_iff` at 151 and 160 crosses the same defeq a second time, since the RHS `σ.toLeft ∈ K` is stated at the abstract level while the Pre lemma states it at the precomplex level.

summary: The abstract-layer proofs repeat an undocumented `change` five times to identify membership in an `AbstractSimplicialComplex` with membership in its underlying precomplex, relying on defeq between two distinct `SetLike` instances instead of a stated lemma. Everything in the `PreAbstractSimplicialComplex` namespace is fine.
